title: Tiny Parham and Al Wynn at the Dreamland; the recordings
summary: Sorting out the sequence of bands, Punch explains the twelve-piece Dreamland band run by Wynn and Parham, who made records and shared men.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Well that's all very confusing to me because there's too many bands. Like, you worked with Tiny Palm some, didn't you?
Yeah, but this was a little after this.
Well that was after Huey Swift? Yeah. And after Francois? Yeah.

Tiny Palm was after Francois? No, Tiny Palm was a little before Francois. See, I don't know if it, I don't know if it was Tiny Palm Band or Al when band, but they both was there together. See, you know, I think it was Tiny Palm, but Al when was doing a lot of managing, you know. But I'm pretty sure it was Tiny Palm Band, see.
Where at? At the Dreamland in Chicago. That's your first job on then?

Well yeah, I had a first job I went on in Chicago outside of the Miramac Miramaker show. Yeah. We was working at the Monogram Theater, but I was Dublin. I would leave there and go into the Dreamland right across the street, see, and play there with them. Yeah. So it sort of had two leaders in, really, huh? Well yeah, Al when was doing the hiring, I know that, he hired me. Mm-hmm. But Tiny Palm was writing all the music and taking everything else. How big a band was that? Well then they had something like twelve pieces. Mm-hmm. Yeah, they had big bands then.

Was that when you made the recordings with Palm? Yeah, yeah, same time. Mm-hmm. Mm-hmm. So, uh, you might have had some of the same men on the Palm records that you had on the Al Wynn records. That's a possibility.
Yeah, yeah. All be out of the same band. Yeah, this Hopskin fellow, he was using two trumpets then all the time. And he was there still all the time, see. He was Tiny right-hand man.
Yeah, I see. Now, the drummer though was Snaggs, you say, huh?
While I was there, I know you were. Mm-hmm. Yeah.
